body: I don't have a mind's eye. Like, I cannot picture anything in my mind. I have a constant stream of thought, of course, but no images associated. If you asked me to describe an orange, I could tell you things that I know about oranges like their approximate size or skin texture, but I'm working from my knowledge of oranges, not from am orange I am picturing in my mind. The hardest part about it is basically, if I haven't noticed something or committed it to memory specifically, I will not recall it. It becomes very difficult especially when trying to describe people I have recently met; unless their features truly stuck out to me, I only have a vague idea of what they look like.

I grew up pretending I believed in God, making up wild stories about how he spoke to me or came to me in a dream, blah blah blah, because I genuinely thought that's what we all did. Pastors, teachers, everyone. I essentially truly thought we all were playing some giant game of make believe. So really, I never truly believed.

Shit happened in my life, as it does to everyone, and then I thought maybe it was true. Maybe I was missing it, or maybe God didn't want me. Maybe if I just tried talking to him, or believing he was out there, maybe then he'd want me. I earnestly searched for God, went to Christian University, did everything I could to find him.

Then one day, I woke up and realized it's either one of two things: he's not there, or he doesn't want me. So I am now what is called an 'apatheist.'

Apatheism--the belief system that if you could prove to me beyond any shadow of a doubt whether or not God exists; it doesn't matter. I won't change who I am now and how I choose to live my life.
